c.tagline: Isan's gateway city, guarding the Khorat Plateau at the edge of Khao Yai's jungle.

taxi.color: no standard livery (tuk-tuks and songthaews dominate)
taxi.fareNote: Few metered taxis operate outside Bangkok; agree the fare with tuk-tuk, motorbike-taxi, or songthaew drivers before departing.

emergency.note: 112 also works from mobile phones nationwide; English-speaking operators are more likely on the Tourist Police line.

hood_desc: The moated historic core around the Thao Suranaree (Yamo) Monument and Chumphon Gate, Korat's most walkable and touristed quarter; best for first-time visitors wanting temples, the old walls, and easy orientation.
The modern commercial strip along Highway 2 anchored by malls like Terminal 21 Korat and Central Korat; good for shopping, cinemas, and international chain comforts.
The railway quarter around Thanon Chira Junction station where the Bangkok-bound and Isan lines split, with cheap noodle shops and guesthouses catering to travelers in transit.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water, as locals do.

transit.hours: Songthaews and tuk-tuks generally operate from early morning until around 8-9 PM; there is no formal city bus network.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash; songthaews charge a low flat fare per route, while tuk-tuks and motorbike taxis are negotiated per trip.
transit.note: Korat has no metro, tram, or formal public bus system; getting around relies on songthaews, tuk-tuks, motorbike taxis, and increasingly ride-hailing apps.

air: Nakhon Ratchasima Airport has no scheduled commercial flights
Nearest major airport is Suvarnabhumi (BKK) in Bangkok, about 260 km away
train: Nakhon Ratchasima Railway Station on the Bangkok-Nong Khai/Ubon Ratchathani line
High-speed rail line to Bangkok planned for 2027
bus: Korat Bus Terminal 2, with services across Isan, to Bangkok, Laos, and the Cambodian border

ride.avail: limited, usually pre-booked for long distance

tip.r: Not customary at street food stalls or markets; rounding up or leaving small change is appreciated at restaurants, and larger hotels/restaurants often add a 10% service charge already.

food.name: Pad mee Korat

places.name: House of Kin Korat

food.name: Som tam Korat
food.desc: The local papaya salad hybrid: peanuts and dried shrimp like the Thai version plus fermented fish pla ra like the Lao one.

places.name: Kaiyang Nai Mueang
places.note: Isan standby with English translations; som tam here is properly funky with pla ra and seriously spicy.

places.name: Gai Yang Saeng Thai

places.name: Klang Plaza 2 evening stalls
places.note: Evening som tam vendors pound several styles including the Korat version.

food.name: Gai yang (Isan grilled chicken)
food.desc: Chicken marinated in garlic, coriander root and fish sauce, grilled slowly over charcoal and eaten with sticky rice and tamarind dip.

places.name: Gai Yang Saeng Thai
places.note: Korat institution known for juicy rotisserie birds sold whole or by the half.

places.name: Kaiyang Nai Mueang
places.note: Named for its grilled chicken; reliable choice for a first Isan meal in the city.

food.desc: Fat, coiled fermented pork-and-rice sausage grilled over coals and eaten with raw cabbage, ginger slivers and bird's eye chillies.

places.name: Save One Night Market
places.note: Charcoal sausage carts line the market entrance every evening.

places.name: Thao Suranaree Monument food stalls
places.note: Street vendors around the Ya Mo monument grill sausage from late afternoon.

places.name: Wat Boon Night Bazaar
places.note: Several vendors sell the sour Korat-style sausage by the skewer.

food.name: Khanom jeen nam ya
food.desc: Soft fermented rice noodles doused in fish curry and piled with free herbs, pickled greens and raw vegetables; a Korat breakfast staple.

places.name: Khanom Jeen Kru Yot
places.note: Specialist shop serving the noodles with a choice of four curry broths.

places.name: Wat Boon Night Bazaar
places.note: Evening khanom jeen stalls with self-serve herb trays.

food.name: Larb and nam tok
food.desc: Minced or sliced pork and beef salads tossed with toasted rice powder, lime, chilli and mint, scooped up with sticky rice.

places.name: Kaiyang Nai Mueang
places.note: Full Isan salad list alongside the grill; ask for medium heat if you are new to it.

places.name: Save One Night Market
places.note: Cheap plastic-stool Isan stalls turning out larb late into the night.

food.name: Khao Yai wine
food.desc: Thailand's best-known wine region sits just up the road from Korat, producing crisp Chenin Blanc and Shiraz in the tropical highlands.

places.name: GranMonte Vineyard
places.note: Family estate with tastings and a restaurant; the most awarded winery in the province.

places.name: PB Valley Khao Yai Winery

food.name: Oliang and cha yen
food.desc: Old-school Thai iced coffee brewed through a cloth sock and sweet orange iced tea with condensed milk, sold from carts all day.

places.name: Wat Boon Night Bazaar
places.note: Drink carts throughout the bazaar pour both to take away in a bag.

places.name: Save One Night Market

landmarks: Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo)
Korat's beloved heroine statue commands the city gate plaza, wreathed in garlands from devotees who credit her with saving the city in 1826.
Phimai Historical Park (Prasat Hin Phimai)
An hour away, this magnificent Khmer sanctuary of pink sandstone towers rivals Angkor's temples and predates Angkor Wat itself.
Chumphon Gate (Pratu Chumphon)
The last surviving original gate of the seventeenth-century city walls stands floodlit beside Thao Suranari, a proud relic of fortress-era Korat.
Wat Salaloi
A strikingly modern riverside temple shaped like a Chinese junk, founded by Thao Suranari herself and famed for its award-winning ceramic-tiled ordination hall.
Khao Yai National Park
Thailand's oldest national park sprawls across misty mountains southwest of the city, sheltering wild elephants, gibbons, hornbills and thundering waterfalls.
Sai Ngam Banyan Grove
Near Phimai, a 350-year-old banyan tree has spread into a shady labyrinth of trunks and roots covering more than an acre.
Wat Phra Narai Maharat
This central temple enshrines a revered Khmer-era sandstone statue of Vishnu and the city pillar shrine, making it Korat's spiritual heart.
Dan Kwian Pottery Village
A craft village on the Mun River famed for centuries for its distinctive rust-colored, iron-rich pottery sold from workshops lining the road.
Maha Wirawong National Museum
Set in a monastery garden, this quiet museum displays Khmer sculpture, ancient ceramics and Buddhist art collected by a revered local abbot.
Save One Night Market
One of Isan's biggest night markets, a neon-lit sprawl of sizzling street food, bargain fashion and live music beloved by locals.

train.note: No international trains from Korat itself - the Laos crossing is further north at Nong Khai. Nakhon Ratchasima is the junction of the north-eastern network, with trains to Bangkok in about 4-5 hours and services splitting toward Ubon Ratchathani and Nong Khai. A Bangkok-Nakhon Ratchasima high-speed line is under construction. Book on the SRT D-Ticket site up to 90 days ahead.

bus.note: No international coaches from Korat - Laos services run via Nong Khai or Mukdahan. Terminal 2 north of the centre is the main hub, with very frequent buses to Bangkok's Mo Chit (about 3-4 hours on the motorway), Khon Kaen and Ubon Ratchathani on Transport Co. (https://www.transport.co.th/) and Nakhonchai Air. Book through 12Go (https://12go.asia/).

ferry.note: Nakhon Ratchasima is inland on the Khorat plateau with no navigable water, so there are no ferries.
